local.name: qwen3-coder-next
local.description: 80B MoE (3B active) — top-ranked local coding model. 70.6% SWE-Bench Verified. Requires 35-46GB VRAM.

local.name: glm-4.7-flash
local.description: Zhipu AI Flash MoE (30B/3B active). 73.8% SWE-Bench Verified. Strong coding and general intelligence. Use tag glm-4.7-flash (bare glm-4.7 does not resolve on Ollama).

local.name: qwen3:30b-a3b
local.description: MoE hybrid — 30B total, only 3B active per token. Fast as a 3B model, accurate as a 30B. Top performer in April 2026 E2E matrix across tool calling, context retention, and code gen. Best overall local model for the price/speed/quality triangle.

local.name: nemotron-3-super:120b
local.description: Nvidia Nemotron 3 Super — 120B total, 12B active MoE. 256K context, reasoning ON/OFF, strong agentic tool calling. Requires multi-GPU or high-VRAM workstation (~87GB download). NVIDIA Open Model License.

local.name: nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b
local.description: Nvidia Nemotron 3 Nano — 31.6B MoE, only 3.6B active per token. 1M context, reasoning ON/OFF with thinking-budget, strong native agentic tool calling. Fast as a 3B model on a single consumer GPU; direct competitor to Qwen3 30B-A3B and GLM-4.7.

local.name: nemotron-3-nano:4b
local.description: Nvidia Nemotron 3 Nano 4B — compact entry in the Nemotron 3 line. 256K context, reasoning ON/OFF, native tool calling. Runs in ~3 GB VRAM. Good fit for resource-constrained agentic deployments.

local.name: nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-a3b-q4_K_M
local.description: Nvidia's hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE + full-attention model, 30B total / 3B active. 1M native context. Ollama's own q4_K_M quantization (25GB) -- no Q4_K_M quant is published on the official ggml-org HF GGUF repo, so this tag is Ollama-specific and distinct from the llama.cpp catalog's Q4_0/Q8_0 entry. License: OpenMDW-1.1 (openmdw.ai/license/1-1/), not the NVIDIA Open Model License.

local.name: qwen3:30b
local.description: Dense 30B model. Slower than the a3b MoE variant above but may be more consistent on narrow tasks.

local.name: qwen3-coder:30b
local.description: Dense 30B Qwen3 specialized for coding. Strong on agentic file edits and tool use. Smaller cousin of Qwen3 Coder Next; better fit for 24 GB GPUs that can't run the 80B MoE.

local.name: qwen3:32b
local.description: Dense 32B Qwen3 — one tier up from 30B with slightly more capacity. Good general-purpose pick for 24 GB GPUs.

local.name: qwen3.6:35b
local.description: Qwen3.6 35B MoE (3B active) — fast as a 3B model but draws on 35B total capacity. Companion to qwen3.6:27b; the MoE variant for users who want higher throughput on large-context agentic tasks.

local.name: qwen3.6:27b
local.description: Dense 27B Qwen3.6 (Apr 2026). Beats the Qwen3.5 397B flagship on agentic coding while running on a single consumer GPU. The highest-value local pick for Code mode at this tier.

local.name: qwen3.5:27b
local.description: Newer Qwen3.5 generation 27B. Strong general-purpose chat + reasoning. Comfortable on 24 GB at 8K context.

local.name: qwen2.5-coder:32b
local.description: The coding gold standard for local inference. Excellent on edits, refactors, and FIM autocomplete. Native FIM tokens supported. Best 32B coding model widely available.

local.name: deepseek-r1:32b
local.description: Deep reasoning with extended chain-of-thought. Rivals GPT-4 on technical tasks.

local.name: llama3.3:70b
local.description: Meta's flagship. Excellent reasoning, tool use, and code. 111M+ downloads.

local.name: deepseek-r1:70b
local.description: State-of-the-art open reasoning. Deep chain-of-thought with code generation.

local.name: llama4:maverick

local.name: llama4-scout
local.description: Meta's 109B MoE (17B active). Fast with 512K context. Multimodal vision.

local.name: deepseek-v3

local.name: qwen2.5-coder:14b

local.name: qwen3:14b

local.name: deepseek-r1:14b
